data.function: P2 report: Servo rail clamp response and overshoot
data.ruling: The refutation stands. The claim says its response times start at the threshold and include the op-amp's 0.33 us overload recovery and its 2 V/us slew. They do not. CSD17578Q3A: 3.1 us to conduction and 15.6 us to 4.5 V. NTTFS4C10NTAG: 1.9 us and 9.8 us. Each of these is the 3.92 kOhm gate RC driven by an instant 4.9 V step, with no recovery and no slew (clamp.py, response block). With both included, the CSD17578Q3A gate reaches VGS(th) max 1.9 V at 4.65 us and 4.5 V at 17.21 us after the threshold. The NTTFS4C10NTAG gate gets there at 3.53 us and 11.37 us, using its 993 pF typical Ciss, as the datasheet gives no maximum. So the response times are understated by 1.6 us to conduction on both parts and by 1.6 to 1.6 us to full enhancement. The overshoot figures were computed over 17 us, not over the stated 15.6 us, so the claim contradicts itself. They match the corrected time to within rounding: 0.108 V into 1000 uF, 0.230 V into 470 uF and 1.08 V into 100 uF at 17 us, against 0.109 V, 0.233 V and 1.09 V at 17.2 us. The overshoot values hold. The response-time values in the figure do not. This concerns the figure in this function, not any part's lifecycle or identity, so the scope is function.
data.evidence:
Datasheet values re-read. OPA376 (SBOS406G), Electrical Characteristics: slew rate 2 V/us typical at G=1, overload recovery time 0.33 us typical. CSD17578Q3A (SLPS525A, revised January 2016), section 5.1: VGS(th) 1.1 / 1.5 / 1.9 V min/typ/max at VDS = VGS and ID = 250 uA; Ciss 1150 pF typical, 1590 pF maximum. NTTFS4C10N/D: Ciss 993 pF typical, no maximum; VGS(TH) 1.3 to 2.2 V.

Model re-run at 2026-10-03T02:18:36Z. P2's clamp.py is identical to the verifier's copy, which `diff` confirms. It computes tau x ln(4.9/(4.9 - Vg)) with tau = 3.92 kOhm x 1.59 nF = 6.23 us. That gives 3.06 us at 1.9 V and 15.62 us at 4.5 V, and 1.91 us and 9.75 us for the NTTFS4C10NTAG. These are the claimed values, and the formula has no delay term and no ramp term.

The verifier's resp.py, a 1 ns Euler step with a 0.33 us delay and a 2 V/us ramp to 4.9 V, gives 1.9 V at 4.7 us and 4.5 V at 17.2 us. My own closed-form first-order solution (ramp, then hold, into the RC) gives the same: 4.65 us and 17.21 us for the CSD17578Q3A, and 3.53 us and 11.37 us for the NTTFS4C10NTAG.

Overshoot, I x t / C at 6.35 A:
- over 17 us: 0.108 V into 1000 uF, 0.230 V into 470 uF, 1.079 V into 100 uF
- over 17.2 us: 0.109 V, 0.233 V and 1.09 V

The model files are /home/claude/rcbench-research/round2/scratch/FU-2I/P2-R6/model/clamp.py and /home/claude/rcbench-research/round2/scratch/FU-2I/P4-datasheet-R6/model/resp.py. The datasheet text is saved in /home/claude/rcbench-research/round2/scratch/FU-2I/adjudicator-R6/.
